general_information.Description: The course provides a better understanding of emerging new technologies (AI) as well as digital and legacy media by guiding students through the development and implementation of a comprehensive Integrated Marketing Communication (IMC) plan for businesses and organizations. Along with knowledge of IMC's crucial elements such as market analysis, creative conceptualization, target audience, brand positioning, intensity of advertising, sales promotion, public relations, etc., the course helps provide students with a comprehensive understanding of IMC in digital age by emphasizing the importance of social media, website development, search engine optimization, mobile marketing, brand promotion events, and retail store connectivity. Upon successful completion of this course, students shall: 1. Gain a comprehensive understanding of the theoretical foundations of IMC and its role in brand building and growth. 2. Demonstrate proficiency in using tools, software, and AI for data analysis and multimedia creation to enhance IMC plans. 3. Demonstrate strong analytical skills essential for overcoming challenges in marketing operations and making informed decisions. 4. Develop, implement, and evaluate a comprehensive IMC plan while considering ethical, privacy, and cultural factors.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be eligible for the final examination. - Students are responsible for completing all exercises, questions, assignments given by instructor(s)/ lecturer(s) in class or at home and submit on time - Laptops may be used in class solely for learning purposes. - Students must promptly access the FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand the theoretical foundations of IMC and its role in brand building and company growth.
Demonstrate proficiency in using tools, software, and AI for data analysis or multimedia creation to enhance the effectiveness of IMC plans.
Develop, implement, and evaluate a comprehensive IMC plan and message strategically.
Understand ethical, privacy, and cultural considerations, as well as social responsibility, in the development and execution of IMC strategies.
Have the ability to work independently or collaboratively with a high level of professionalism, both in academic pursuits and practical applications

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Participation grade will be given based on students' attendance, students' attitude, preparation, contribution of discussions

assessments.Question Type: Opt.1: Group Project (Case Study Approach)Suggested Topic: Select a real-world case study focused on a company’s marketing communications efforts.Task:- Analyze the company’s existing IMC strategy and tactics, identifying strengths and weaknesses.- Evaluate the effectiveness of the campaign using course frameworks (Strategic Integrated Marketing Communications, Percy & Rosenbaum-Elliott).- Integrate AI tools at multiple stages:++ Secondary Research & Benchmarking – AI-assisted competitor analysis, trend monitoring, market scanning.++ Customer & Audience Insights – AI analytics tools (e.g., Brandwatch, ChatGPT, Google Gemini) for segmentation, persona generation, sentiment analysis.++ Message & Content Testing – AI-generated draft messages, ad copies, or visuals; A/B testing simulations.++ Media Planning – AI scheduling or channel optimization (Buffer AI, Hootsuite, SEMRush, etc.).++ Evaluation & KPIs – AI dashboards to measure engagement, reach, conversion, and sentiment.Opt.2: Group Project (Constructivism Approach)Task: Follow lecturers’ proposal for a guided IMC project.- Students will collaborate under the lecturer’s direction on a selected brand, campaign, or thematic issue.- AI tools will be incorporated into guided exercises at each stage: persona building, content creation, campaign evaluation.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Duration: 5 WeeksType: Group Project (Max 4–5 members)Deliverables: Written Report + Campaign Proposal + PresentationTask DescriptionStudents will act as an IMC agency team tasked with designing and presenting a fully integrated marketing communication (IMC) campaign for a real brand, product, service, or NGO initiative in the digital environment.The campaign must demonstrate:- Strategic alignment with brand positioning.- Creative integration across communication channels.- Measurable business and communication impact.- Responsible and transparent use of AI tools in research, content creation, execution, and evaluation.Each group may either:- Work with a real client (brand or NGO) and co-develop an IMC campaign.- Choose from a list of provided cases/issues and design a digital-first IMC plan.- Propose a self-selected brand or issue (with instructor approval).- Campaign Proposal Requirements- Executive Summary – overview of campaign concept, objectives, and AI integration highlights.- Situation Analysis – SWOT/PESTLE, competitive benchmarking, and AI-assisted market research (validated by human judgment).- Target Audience & Customer Personas – developed through AI-based analytics (e.g., Brandwatch, ChatGPT, Google Gemini) and refined by team insights.- Campaign Goal & SMART Objectives – clear marketing and communication outcomes.- Key Messages & Storytelling Strategy – alignment with brand voice, adapted for multicultural and digital contexts.- IMC Strategies & Tactics – covering the full spectrum of communication mix, supported by AI tools:++ Advertising (AI-assisted copywriting, visuals, video generation).++ Sales Promotion (AI-powered customer segmentation and targeting).++ Digital/Social Media (AI scheduling, SEO, influencer analysis).++ Public Relations (AI-assisted press kit, sentiment analysis).++ Direct & Interactive Marketing (personalized email/CRM content using AI).++ Creative Samples – mockups, AI-generated content, or prototypes of campaign assets.++ Media & Channel Integration Plan – explain how AI supports message consistency across touchpoints.++ Risk Analysis – potential ethical/privacy issues, AI bias risks, and contingency strategies.++ Budget & Resource Plan – realistic allocation, noting AI tools used for efficiency.++ Evaluation & Metrics – campaign success indicators (engagement, reach, conversion, sentiment, SEO rankings), with AI dashboards for measurement.- Execution Phase (Optional, if feasible)++ May include social media activations, influencer collaborations, digital events, or cross-platform storytelling.AI may be used for asset design, predictive audience targeting, automated scheduling, and real-time performance monitoring—but all outputs must be transparently reported and fact-checked.Deliverables:1. Campaign Proposal Report (max 20 pages):- Situation analysis, objectives, IMC strategies & tactics.- Sample content pieces (with clear AI vs. human contribution).- Integration strategy across platforms.- Campaign evaluation framework.2. Presentation Deck:- Key highlights of campaign strategy, creative outputs, and AI integration.3. Reflection Section (300–500 words per group):- How AI was applied, benefits, limitations, risks, and ethical considerations.
assessments.Grading Guide: According to the predetermined LOs, lecturers have the flexibility to choose assignment forms. Each assignment has a six-day due date, which commences when the lecturers provides detailed instructions. AI is treated as a support tool; human strategic thinking, creativity, and ethical responsibility remain central. All AI-generated outputs must be fact-checked, critically evaluated, and transparently reported. Projects will be graded on: Theoretical application (IMC frameworks), Analytical depth, Creativity, AI integration, Ethical awareness, and Professional presentation. Notes: - Students must show mastery of IMC theories and frameworks (Kliatchko, Percy & Rosenbaum-Elliott, etc.). - AI is a support tool; human creativity, cultural sensitivity, and ethical responsibility remain central. - All AI-generated insights or content must be verified, adapted, and contextualized before use. - Campaigns will be graded on strategic depth, creativity, integration, AI literacy, and professionalism.
assessments.Note: Assess the knowledge students have acquired in class up to the time of the assignment.

assessments.Question Type: Opt.1: Case Analysis Approach Task: Conduct a comprehensive analysis of a selected brand’s Integrated Marketing Communications (IMC) strategy, applying course theories and AI-supported tools. Students are required to: - Examine messaging consistency across platforms (TV, print, social media, website, influencers, etc.). - Evaluate the IMC approach in terms of: - Target audience segmentation & engagement. - Brand positioning & competitive differentiation. - Alignment with overall marketing objectives. Integrate AI tools at different stages: - Secondary Research: AI-supported competitor benchmarking and trend scanning. - Message Audit: AI clustering of brand messages to detect consistency/inconsistency. - Audience Insight: AI analytics (e.g., Brandwatch, ChatGPT, Gemini) for audience perceptions or sentiment analysis. - Content Testing: AI-assisted drafting of alternative message variations and engagement prediction. Opt.2: Constructivism Approach Task: Students follow the lecturer’s proposal for an IMC-focused assignment, designed as a step-by-step AI-assisted task. Possible activities include: - Building an AI-generated customer persona for a chosen brand and refining it with human insights. - Producing a short AI-assisted IMC content sample (e.g., social media post, video, infographic) aligned with course theories. - Evaluating a campaign’s AI-powered performance metrics (e.g., reach, sentiment, SEO visibility).
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Practice 1 – Buyer Persona & Mini IMC Plan (AI-Supported) Task: Students will be required to create a buyer persona for their most loved brand, applying IMC theories discussed in class and AI-supported tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Brandwatch, audience insight platforms). This practice helps students: - Identify basic IMC concepts (brand positioning, brand-consumer relationship, audience segmentation). - Understand how AI can assist in consumer research and persona creation. - Translate insights into a mini IMC plan (content mission, type, platform). AI Use: - Generate draft personas. - Visualize customer profiles. - Simulate audience responses. Deliverables: - Buyer persona profile (AI-generated draft + human-refined version). - Mini IMC content plan (mission, type, format, platform). - Reflection (300–500 words) on AI use, benefits, risks, and ethical considerations. Practice 2 – AI-Assisted IMC Content Creation Task: Students will develop a media product related to IMC, using AI-powered tools (e.g., Canva AI, Midjourney, Runway for visuals/video; ChatGPT for copywriting; ElevenLabs for voice). Possible outputs: - Social media post. - Short video / podcast snippet. - Infographic. - Interactive digital content. Deliverables: - Final media product (with clear indication of AI vs. human input). - Reflection Report (500–700 words) covering: - AI application process (tools, steps, outcomes). - Benefits & limitations of AI in content creation. - Ethical considerations (bias, copyright, transparency).
assessments.Grading Guide: According to the predetermined LOs, lecturers have the flexibility to choose assignment forms. Each assignment has a six-day due date, which commences when the lecturers provides detailed instructions. Students are allowed to adopt AI-assisted tools to enhance the effectiveness of their work. They may be asked to submit prompts, and/or AI-generated outputs, and/or a brief reflection explaining how they used the tools and evaluated the outputs. Assignments must explicitly connect to IMC theories and frameworks covered in class (Kliatchko’s IMC, Percy & Rosenbaum-Elliott, brand touchpoints). AI is a supportive tool: students must show where it was used, how it added value, and how they critically evaluated its accuracy and ethics. Submissions will be graded on: Theoretical depth, Analytical rigor, Creativity, AI integration, Ethical awareness, and Report quality.
